available_governed_components.boundary: First-person role is scoped; no global person paradigm.
Current approved use is scoped L01 negation/absence; L02 extension requires separate review.
PA means lexical 'ontem' only and must not be converted into a generic past marker.

evidence_support.supports: NE can participate in scoped predicate-negation behavior
evidence_support.does_not_support: Negative past or L02 declarative order

evidence_support.supports: PA may appear as lexical yesterday anchor in one validated L02 question
evidence_support.does_not_support: Generic past tense or declarative temporal syntax

evidence_support.supports: First-person referent for scoped L01/L02 use
evidence_support.does_not_support: Exact declarative subject position for this new frame

unresolved_design_questions: Should NE be extended to L02 for this structure?
What exact declarative ordering, if any, is permitted for AN + NEGATION + PREDICATE?
Should PA be present only in examples meaning literally 'yesterday', rather than inside the abstract I-didn't frame?
Which already governed predicate(s) may instantiate the first course example without implying a generic DID auxiliary?
prohibited_shortcuts: Do not equate English DID with a new HNK auxiliary.
Do not promote PA from 'ontem' to PAST.
Do not assume AN NE PREDICATE or PA AN NE PREDICATE word order without a separate pattern gate.
Do not invent a new negation or tense lexeme to fill the numerical slot.
